coreIdea: DFA=one transition per state-symbol. NFA=multiple/zero+ε allowed. Equally powerful (both = regular languages). Trace short strings to identify language; design around a tracked state-variable to construct.
mustRememberFormulas: NFA n states → DFA ≤2^n states (subset construction)
Complement = swap accept/reject, ONLY on a COMPLETE DFA (add trap state first)
Count length-n accepted strings = sum of (TransitionMatrix^n)[start][accepting states]

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: state diagram given, asked what language it accepts
language description given, asked to construct DFA/NFA
complement/product/union of automata, or NFA-vs-DFA power claim

commonTrapsQuickList: Complementing an INCOMPLETE DFA without adding a trap state first gives the wrong answer
NFA and DFA are EQUALLY powerful — NFA is more concise, never more expressive
For NFA tracing, track the full SET of possible states, not just one path
Testing too few example strings before generalizing the accepted language
highYieldPyqLessons: Identify-the-language (13/43) and equivalence/closure-operations (13/43) are tied as the biggest sub-skills — together over 60% of the topic.
